title: Fines for Building Off-Design or Hiring Unqualified Workers 2026
desc: Decree 339/2026/ND-CP fines for homeowners hiring unqualified designers or builders, and contractors who build off-design or borrow certificates.
summary: Fines for homeowners and contractors who build contrary to the design, assign work to people lacking expertise or capability, or borrow practicing certificates, under Decree 339/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

Hiring a crew of "acquaintances" without expertise, or workers who change the structure on their own to be "quick and cheap", is behind many housing incidents. From 26 August 2026, Decree 339/2026/ND-CP sets separate fines for these acts, for both homeowners and contractors.
h2
1. Rules on who designs and builds houses
ul

A homeowner may design their own detached house only if it meets all of the following: fewer than 3 floors, no basement, total floor area under 250 m², and height under 12 m; otherwise it must be done by an organization or individual with expertise and experience (Clause 2, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP). See also Designing your own house: when must you hire a design firm?.
Construction must comply with the approved design, regulations, and standards and use materials as the design requires (Clauses 1 and 4, Article 50 of the Construction Law 2025).
The contractor is responsible for quality in line with the design, including work done by subcontractors (Points c and l, Clause 2, Article 61).
Changing an assessed and approved design on one's own in a way that affects construction safety or fire safety is prohibited (Clause 10, Article 15).
h2
2. How to read the fines
p

The fines in the decree are the amounts for organizations; an individual committing the same act is fined half. The act in Clause 1, Article 13 (below) is the exception: that amount applies directly to individuals (Clause 4, Article 5).
h2
3. Fines for homeowners
ul

Allowing an organization or individual without the expertise and experience required to design, build, or supervise a detached house: VND 20–40 million (Point c, Clause 2, Article 22), that is, VND 10–20 million for an individual.

Building not in accordance with a new construction permit: VND 30–40 million for a detached house, plus a requirement to apply to adjust the permit or demolish the non-compliant part (Clauses 6 and 14, Article 25). For details see Fines for building without a permit or contrary to a permit.
h2
4. Fines for contractors and builders
ul
Building not in accordance with the contract or design: VND 40–60 million, plus a requirement to build in accordance with the design (Point đ, Clause 3, and Point n, Clause 5, Article 23).
Failing to deploy personnel and equipment as the contract requires; failing to carry out material tests and checks required by the design: VND 40–60 million (Points c and e, Clause 3, Article 23).
No construction log, or one prepared contrary to regulations: VND 10–20 million (Point c, Clause 1, Article 23).

A contractor that assigns people who do not meet the capability requirements to positions as required, or fails to publish capability information: VND 20–40 million, and is also suspended from construction activity for 1 to 3 months (Clauses 2 and 4, Article 13).

An individual carrying out construction activity without meeting the requirements, or borrowing, lending, renting, or renting out a practicing certificate: VND 10–20 million; borrowing or renting a certificate also results in the certificate being revoked for 6 to 12 months (Clauses 1 and 4, Article 13).
h2
5. Limitation period and advice for homeowners
p

The limitation period for penalizing violations in the construction field is 2 years; for detached houses, the time a violation ends is the date the house is put into use (or the completion date stated in the construction contract if that cannot be determined) (Article 6).
ol
Hire design and construction firms with expertise and experience suited to the size of the house; check their capability information before signing.
State in the contract: construction follows the approved drawings, and any change requires written consent from the homeowner and the designer.
Require the contractor to keep a construction log and have each part (foundation, columns, floors) accepted before continuing.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The fines above apply to detached houses outside heritage and relic areas. Specific capability conditions and practicing certificates are governed by Decree 212/2026/ND-CP.
